title: 2.4 Consequences of Climate Change
description: Warming trends, precipitation shifts, sea level rise, polar change and ecosystem impacts. Easy level.

questions.question: By about how much has average global surface air temperature risen since the late 1800s?
options: Up to three times as much

questions.question: Which areas warm faster than the global average?
options: Land areas, especially at northern high latitudes in winter
Dark forests absorb more sunlight than snow, accelerating warming
Tropical regions where many developing nations are located
Warmer air holds more snow inland while coastal melting increases
questions.correctAnswer: Land areas, especially at northern high latitudes in winter

questions.question: What generally happens to sea level as land ice melts and oceans warm?
By about how much did global sea level rise in the twentieth century?
options: Up to three times as much

questions.question: What share of sea level rise came from melting glaciers and ice sheets?
What is a likely consequence of higher sea level for coastal areas?
options: Expansion of oceans as they warm
Up to three times as much

questions.question: Which polar region is described as experiencing rapid melting of ice and snow?
In which years did Arctic sea ice reach dramatic record lows?
What may happen to tropical crop yields as the climate warms?
options: Up to three times as much

questions.question: What can elevated carbon dioxide do for some plants?
options: More frequent dry spells in forested areas
Rising seas push salt into freshwater aquifers
Act as a fertilizer and speed up growth
Longer growing seasons and earlier snowmelt
questions.correctAnswer: Act as a fertilizer and speed up growth
